title: Updates.reloadAsync() crashes if called during first startup
body: I use `Updates.reloadAsync()` on account removal or logout so no reducer state remains. In an iOS production build on Expo SDK 47, calling it directly during the app's first launch crashes the app. After reopening the same app, the same call works. Android does not appear to crash. If an update is available, the sequence `checkForUpdateAsync()`, `fetchUpdateAsync()`, then `reloadAsync()` can reload successfully, but a later direct `reloadAsync()` during that first launch can still crash. Restarting the app once avoids the crash. This is a managed Expo app using Expo 47.0.13 and React Native 0.70.5.

symptoms_visible: On iOS, calling `Updates.reloadAsync()` directly during the first launch closes the production app.
After I reopen the app, the same `reloadAsync()` call works.
Android does not appear to crash in the same flow.
N0.label: N0 first-launch iOS reload crash reported

symptoms_visible: A blank SDK 47 app with expo-updates crashes when I press a control that calls `reloadAsync()` on its first launch; after reopening it, pressing the same control reloads normally.
The iOS failure is a SIGABRT with a JSCRuntime assertion about a dangling API object.
N1.label: N1 minimal SDK 47 reproduction and crash signature

symptoms_visible: In my new SDK 48 build, calling `Updates.reloadAsync()` during the first app launch reloads the app without crashing.
The older SDK 47 build still crashes in that first-launch test.
N2.label: N2 SDK 48 candidate build succeeds

symptoms_visible: My successful SDK 48 build uses Hermes.
In another affected SDK 48 app, `reloadAsync()` crashed while the app was configured for JSC and stopped crashing after rebuilding it with Hermes.
N3.label: N3 JavaScript engine comparison collected

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding the affected apps on SDK 48 with Hermes, `Updates.reloadAsync()` works during the first launch without closing the app.
N_terminal.label: terminal first-launch reload verified across affected apps

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the crash in a blank app with only the minimum Expo dependencies and describe the exact steps?
Does a minimal release build still crash if its only action is calling `reloadAsync()`?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I can make a blank SDK 47 app, install and configure expo-updates, add an onPress that calls `Updates.reloadAsync()`, and create an iOS production build. On the first launch, pressing it crashes the app. After reopening the app, pressing the same element works. No pushed update is needed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The blank app never crashes; I can reproduce it only in our full application after several other libraries initialize.
The same blank SDK 47 app reproduces it from a release simulator build rather than a TestFlight installation.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's system, c4, plus the corroborating affected SDK 47 user in c5 folded into the simulated user side. The blank-app steps isolate the opening reporter's direct first-launch reload problem; c5's JSC SIGABRT signature is added as volunteered evidence rather than as an engineer conclusion.

solution.intent: Build the app with Expo SDK 48 and test the same direct `reloadAsync()` action during its first launch.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade the minimal app to Expo SDK 48, make a new iOS build, install it, and invoke the same direct `Updates.reloadAsync()` action during the first launch.

edges.comment: c8-c9 on the opening reporter's chain: another affected developer reports SDK 48 success, then the reporter upgrades, creates a new build, and confirms that direct first-launch reload no longer crashes. This retained SDK upgrade is a persistent system change, not a measurement-only edge.

question_patterns: Which JavaScript runtime is the successful new build using?
What runtime configuration changed between the crashing and non-crashing builds?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The successful SDK 48 build uses Hermes, since that is now the default. The old SDK 47 app was on the previous runtime setup.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both the crashing SDK 47 build and successful SDK 48 build use the same JSC configuration.

question_patterns: Can an affected app compare the behavior under the two available JavaScript runtimes?
Does rebuilding the same affected app with a different JavaScript engine change the first-launch result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In an affected SDK 48 app I had `jsEngine: 'jsc'` configured, and the button-triggered `reloadAsync()` crashed. After changing the build to Hermes, the same action stopped crashing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same app crashes under both JSC and Hermes with no behavioral difference.
Hermes also avoids the crash in an SDK 47 build rather than an SDK 48 build.

edges.comment: c13-c14 establish that the reporter's successful SDK 48 build uses Hermes. c21 contributes the direct JSC-versus-Hermes comparison from another affected app; that affected user is explicitly folded into the simulated user side. This comparison pertains to the same direct button-triggered reload symptom, unlike the separate check/fetch hangs discussed elsewhere in the thread.

solution.intent: Move the affected iOS apps off the JSC configuration by using Hermes, preferably through the SDK 48 upgrade already shown to work, then verify direct first-launch reload in every rebuilt app.
solution.concrete_example: Use Hermes for the iOS build—upgrading to SDK 48 supplies that default in this case—then rebuild and install the app. On a fresh first launch, invoke the same logout or button path that calls `Updates.reloadAsync()` and confirm that the app reloads instead of terminating.
solution.inference_hint: The users supplied the raw observations: a JSC runtime assertion, SDK 48 with Hermes succeeds, and an affected SDK 48 JSC build stops crashing after a Hermes rebuild. Interpreting those observations as a JSC-specific runtime teardown failure in the direct first-launch reload path is engineer-side inference. Do not conflate this chain with the separate early-startup check/fetch race and Android hanging reports later discussed in the thread.

edges.comment: Resolution for the opening reporter per c9, c14 and c17, corroborated by c21: SDK 48/Hermes avoids the direct first-launch reload crash, and the reporter states it was tested across their small and large apps. Later reports about simultaneous automatic/manual update checks, missing update environment variables, Reanimated, and post-reload Android hangs are separate deployment chains and are deliberately excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause at the level established by this chain: the direct first-launch `reloadAsync()` crash follows the iOS JSC runtime path, with the JSC dangling-API-object assertion and the JSC-versus-Hermes comparison grounding that conclusion.
Must recommend rebuilding the affected iOS app with Hermes; upgrading to SDK 48 is the reporter-verified route because that build uses Hermes by default.

Must distinguish this direct logout or button-triggered reload crash from the separate thread problems involving simultaneous native and JavaScript update checks, `fetchUpdateAsync()` or `checkForUpdateAsync()` hangs, update environment variables, Reanimated, and later Android behavior.
Must ask the user to verify the rebuilt app by invoking the same direct `reloadAsync()` path during a fresh first launch before declaring the issue resolved.
Resolution requires the observable confirmation surfaced by the graph: the reporter's affected apps reload during first launch without terminating.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Expo application developer who can create managed production builds, configure expo-updates and JavaScript engines, reduce a problem to a blank app, and compare SDK builds.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, detailed, and persistent; provides exact reproduction steps, distinguishes update-driven reloads from direct reloads, and reports concrete cross-platform and first-launch differences.
